did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm’s title identifies it as belonging to David and places it in the wilderness of Judah, creating from the very beginning a setting of solitude, dryness, and dependence on God.
Did you know? David expresses his longing for God through images of thirst and yearning: not only is his soul thirsty, but his body also longs for Him in a dry and weary land without water.

Did you know? Although he is in the wilderness, David remembers encountering God in the sanctuary and longs to see His power and glory there; this spiritual memory strengthens him in a time of deprivation.
Did you know? David declares that God’s lovingkindness is better than life itself, and therefore his lips will praise God even in the wilderness and in times of distress.
Did you know? Lifting his hands in God’s name expresses an act of blessing, prayer, and thanksgiving—something David pledges to do throughout his life.
Did you know? David uses the imagery of fat and rich food to describe spiritual satisfaction and fullness; he finds this satisfaction in praise and joyful lips.
Did you know? Even during the night, David continues to remember and meditate on God: he mentions his bed and the watches of the night.
Did you know? The image of God as the shadow of His wings presents Him as a source of shelter and protection, after David has already recognized Him as his help.
Did you know? The expression “My soul clings to You” describes a close and continual bond with God, while “Your right hand upholds me” emphasizes that God is the One who supports David.

Did you know? In its final section, the psalm moves from longing and thanksgiving to confrontation with enemies: David describes those who seek his life, mentions their downfall by the sword and their descent to the depths of the earth, and concludes with the king rejoicing in God and the silencing of liars.
